page: Microsoft Azure D192s_v7 is a Dsv7-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 96 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The processor architecture is x86_64, incorporating a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1D cache. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. The Intel Xeon processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions), contribute to high-throughput capabilities, as evidenced by top-tier scores in PassMark extended instructions and encryption tests. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only cached small block transfers reaching 14,141.15 GB/sec and uncached large block writes at 269.25 GB/sec.

While the instance demonstrates strong prompt processing speeds for large language models, text generation speeds are comparatively limited, falling into the bottom tier for smaller models. Single-core performance and PassMark memory scores remain in the average tier. Given the massive parallel processing capacity and high memory bandwidth, this server is suited for heavy multi-threaded workloads, database operations, static web serving, and high-throughput data decompression, rather than single-threaded tasks or local-storage-dependent applications.
